name: Bound keys only: the setting, its audited switch, and a preview that says what it did not decide
summary: bound_keys_only (deployment.private.json; absent/false is off) makes the wrapper refuse a line lacking a project or a principal; the switch (status/on/off, operator-gated, audited) previews what on would cut off. REFUSED (would_be_refused: twenty numbers, _more): the command is EXACTLY what authorized-keys prints - an absolute interpreter path (the first word is trusted, not judged: read it), then BOTH -E and -s, each alone, in that order, then this kit's wrapper (or the wrapper first), plain ASCII, a wrapper path of at most 512 bytes, an absolute --root - and the line is unbound, or bound but refused either way (a relative --endpoint, an ill-formed project name). MAY BE REFUSED (may_be_refused, _more): every other command= line - a bare interpreter name, other flags or order, another wrapper or root, shell syntax, a relative path, another program, a command over 8192 characters. Both are printed BEFORE the write. A bound line naming a well-formed project without a folder is in no group. wrapper_names_setting is a HINT from the wrapper's first 64 KiB (a fifo is opened non-blocking, never read). on REFUSES an unreadable or partly-inspected keys file unless --without-preview is said.
